# PRD: WhatsApp Assistant for Residents

## Problem Statement

Residents miss estate information and reminders because they live on WhatsApp, not on the estate's web surfaces. Exco needs a channel where they can actually reach residents, and residents increasingly expect to transact and check things in chat rather than in a portal. Financially, arrears go uncollected because reminders land in inboxes nobody opens. When a resident does want to know their financial standing, they must call or email the exco — no self-serve path exists.

## Solution

A dedicated WhatsApp Business number operates the estate's **WhatsApp Assistant**: it proactively delivers approved estate information (invoice reminders, payment confirmations, announcements) and, on demand, lets eligible residents peruse their financial standing through a structured menu — balance, last payment, statement, next due, and wallet — in private one-to-one chat, gated by opt-in and an optional PIN.

## User Stories

1. As an eligible resident, I want to message the estate's WhatsApp number and be recognized from my registered phone number, so that I can start using the Assistant without any setup.
2. As an eligible resident with an unrecognized number, I want to link my number via a one-time PIN, so that I can use the Assistant from a phone number not on file.
3. As an eligible resident, I want to consent to WhatsApp alerts during linking, so that I only receive estate broadcasts if I opted in.
4. As a billable resident, I want to see my balance (outstanding across open invoices with an arrears flag), so that I know what I owe at a glance.
5. As a billable resident, I want to see my last payment (amount, date, what it covered), so that I can confirm receipts quickly.
6. As a billable resident, I want to view my statement for a fixed period (this month / this year / last six months), so that I can review my full ledger.
7. As a billable resident, I want to see my next due invoice (amount, due date, line items), so that I can plan payments.
8. As a billable resident, I want to see my wallet balance, so that I know my prepaid position.
9. As a resident holding billable roles on multiple houses, I want to pick which property a financial answer refers to, so that I get per-property truth rather than a mixed answer.
10. As a multi-house resident, I want an all-properties aggregation for my statement, so that I can see my consolidated position in one view.
11. As a resident who opted in, I want my set PIN to gate financial answers, so that a lost or borrowed phone can't read my financial position.
12. As a resident without a PIN, I want financial answers to still work and a gentle nudge offering to set a PIN, so that low-friction access is preserved for non-technical residents.
13. As a resident with a billable role who has NOT opted in, I want identity and consent flow to work but financial answers withheld until I consent, so that the estate stays WhatsApp-compliant.
14. As a resident with a non-billable role (household member, caretaker, staff, contractor), I want estate information (announcements, notices, security updates) but no financial answers, so that I get community value without ledger exposure.
15. As an opted-in resident, I want to text STOP to unsubscribe from broadcasts and START to re-subscribe, so that I control the channel.
16. As an unrostered person, I want a guarded intro that offers onboarding or STOP, so that I'm neither turned away abruptly nor able to guess financial data.
17. As a resident, I want my financial answers to arrive as deterministic menu replies, so that answers are predictable and readable on WhatsApp.
18. As a resident, I want a short PIN-link flow and a 15-minute conversation session, so that interrupted queries resume rather than restarting.
19. As a resident, I want the Assistant to never expose another resident's financial data, so that privacy is preserved in a shared-chat environment.
20. As exco, I want the estate's WhatsApp number to send approved invoice reminders, so that collections improve.
21. As exco, I want a payment-received confirmation on WhatsApp, so that residents see receipts immediately.
22. As exco, I want announcements mirrored to WhatsApp, so that estate news reaches residents where they live.
23. As exco, I want all proactive WhatsApp messages to use pre-approved Meta templates, so that the channel stays compliant.
24. As exco, I want an operational console to view the opt-in registry and bulk-import launch consent, so that I can onboard residents efficiently.
25. As exco, I want a force-PIN toggle, so that I can require PINs estate-wide if security posture tightens.
26. As exco, I want a disclosure-log viewer (searchable by resident/number/date), so that I can audit who saw financial answers.
27. As exco, I want bot health metrics (inbound/outbound counts, delivery failures, template errors), so that I can spot problems early.
28. As exco, I want to inspect and reset stuck sessions, so that a bot loop doesn't wedge a resident.
29. As exco, I want a pending-contacts view, so that I can attach unclaimed numbers to residents.
30. As exco, I want software outbound/lookup caps in system settings, so that a defect can't cause bill shock or a broadcast storm.
31. As an admin, I want every admin write action on the WhatsApp module to require permission and be audited, so that the module follows the estate's security contract.
32. As a developer, I want a WhatsApp simulator harness, so that I can develop the menu without live Meta traffic.
33. As exco, I want a pilot phase (exco/one street) before estate-wide enablement, so that the module is proven on a small base first.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Guardrail exception (ADR-0001):** the WhatsApp Assistant is a deliberate resident-facing surface despite the admin-first guardrail; the web portal remains out of scope.
- **Channel shape (ADR-0002):** Meta WhatsApp Cloud API directly, provider-agnostic behind `src/lib/whatsapp/`; no BSP.
- **Dedicated 1:1 number:** a separate WhatsApp Business number; the existing organic group is untouched.
- **Outbound seam:** implement `sendViaWhatsApp` in the existing notification dispatcher (`src/lib/notifications/send.ts`) and add `whatsapp` to `IMPLEMENTED_CHANNELS`. All existing producers (invoice reminders, announcements, payment events, queue, history, preferences) are reused unchanged. Note: SMS is currently listed in `IMPLEMENTED_CHANNELS` but is NOT actually implemented — correct this discrepancy (either implement or remove) while touching this file.
- **Inbound seam:** single new module `src/lib/whatsapp/`. Public API: `sendWhatsAppMessage()` (used by the dispatcher stub) and `handleInboundMessage()` (called by the webhook route). Everything conversational lives inside: identity resolution, opt-in/PIN gates, menu engine, session, dedup, disclosure logging. Provider SDK and the `/api/whatsapp/webhook` route stay thin.
- **Webhook:** new Next.js route `/api/whatsapp/webhook`; verify Meta `X-Hub-Signature-256` with the app secret; support the `hub.challenge` handshake. A server route (not a server action) — the mandatory permission/audit contract applies to admin write actions, not the inbound handler.
- **Identity resolution:** match inbound number against `phone_primary` / `phone_secondary`; PIN-link flow as fallback for unrostered numbers; unclaimed numbers become pending contacts surfaced in the console.
- **Access model:** identity open to all; financial disclosure gated on opt-in + PIN-if-set; community tier (announcements/notices) for non-billable roles; financial answers only for billable roles.
- **Menu (v1):** Balance, Last payment, Statement, Next due, Wallet. Statement: fixed periods (this month / this year / last six months) with a rolling cap; property-selection step for multi-house residents; optional all-properties aggregation for statements.
- **PIN:** optional per resident; stored hashed; admin force-PIN toggle as a system setting; PIN-less residents get a one-line nudge.
- **Opt-in:** in-chat capture during PIN-link; `whatsapp_optins` registry; STOP/START self-serve; admin bulk-import for launch.
- **Outbound content (v1):** 3 Meta-approved templates — `invoice_reminder`, `payment_received`, `announcement`. Ad-hoc admin blast is post-v1 once templates exist.
- **State & retention:** `whatsapp_sessions` (15-min TTL), `whatsapp_processed_messages` (dedup via wamid, ~24h window), disclosure log (permanent, immutable, entity type `whatsapp_assistant`), pending contacts. Operational state ephemeral; audit permanent.
- **Admin console:** opt-in registry + bulk import, force-PIN toggle, disclosure-log viewer, bot health, session inspector, pending contacts. Admin writes follow `authorizePermission` + `logAudit`; new permission constants; `AuditEntityType` extended.
- **Cost/limits:** per-conversation costs; outbound burst cap + daily lookup cap in `system_settings`.
- **Rollout:** WhatsApp simulator harness in dev → pilot (exco/one street) → estate-wide toggle.

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests assert external behavior through the module's two public entry points (`sendWhatsAppMessage`, `handleInboundMessage`): given an inbound message, the expected reply/state transition occurs — not implementation details of the menu internals.
- **Module tested:** `src/lib/whatsapp/` — identity resolution, opt-in/PIN gating, menu routing, statement composition (fixed periods, property selection, all-properties), session advance/idempotency, dedup, disclosure-log writes, STOP/START, unrostered handling.
- **Dispatcher:** `src/lib/notifications/send.ts` — WhatsApp channel dispatches through `sendViaWhatsApp` when `IMPLEMENTED_CHANNELS` includes `whatsapp`.
- **Admin writes:** module-integration test coverage for new write actions (permission + audit present), following the existing `module-integration.test.ts` pattern with allowlist entries.
- **Prior art:** `src/lib/notifications/__tests__/admin-notifier.test.ts` (unit tests over a notification lib), `src/__tests__/integration/module-integration.test.ts` (structural server-action compliance). E2E harness uses the existing `e2e/` Playwright setup; the WhatsApp simulator replaces live Meta traffic in automated runs.

## Out of Scope

- Ad-hoc admin broadcast composer (post-template add-on).
- Free-text/NLU conversation parsing; LLM assistant.
- Resident web-portal changes (guardrail intact).
- SMS implementation (listed-but-dormant channel; only the `IMPLEMENTED_CHANNELS` discrepancy is fixed here).
- Group-chat integration with the existing WhatsApp group.
- Payment initiation inside the chat (view-only; payments remain on existing paths).
- i18n/localization beyond initial template copy.

## Further Notes

- All proactive messages require pre-approved Meta templates; variable fills go through placeholders. Template copy needs an exco sign-off pass before Meta approval.
- SMS is recorded in `IMPLEMENTED_CHANNELS` but not implemented — resolve this contradiction during the outbound work.
- Financial answers over WhatsApp are not end-to-end encrypted; the PIN layer and disclosure log are the mitigations, and this trade-off is deliberate (ADR-0002 context).
- `CONTEXT.md` glossary defines the canonical terms used here (WhatsApp Assistant, WhatsApp Opt-in, Financial Standing, Billable Role, Eligible Resident, Property Selection, Statement, Community Tier, WhatsApp Session, Disclosure Log, Pending Contact, WhatsApp Template).

## Problem Statement

The Residio admin dashboard has a mature invoice, billing, and bank import engine, but lacks two critical financial operational capabilities: (1) bank reconciliation reporting that shows administrators exactly what was imported vs what was matched after each statement upload, and (2) financial period reports with PDF export, scheduled email delivery, and an interactive dashboard replacing the current thin analytics page.

Administrators currently have no way to verify import accuracy at a glance, no PDF exports for statutory reports, and no scheduled report distribution. The existing analytics page is lightweight and does not cover the financial metrics administrators need.

## Solution

**Bank Reconciliation** — After each bank statement import, the import results step displays a reconciliation summary comparing bank totals (credits/debits) to system totals (payments created/expenses created), with unmatched rows flagged for manual review.

**Financial Reports** — The report engine is extended with PDF rendering. Reports can be generated on-demand (PDF download from the Reports page) or scheduled for automatic email delivery with archive storage. A new financial dashboard replaces the existing analytics page, showing revenue/expense trends, collection health, invoice aging by exact-day histogram, and portfolio value.

**Scheduled Delivery** — Reports configured with a schedule are automatically generated, rendered as PDFs, emailed to configured recipients, and archived in the dashboard for re-download by authorized administrators.

## User Stories

1. As an administrator, I want to see a reconciliation summary after each bank statement import so that I can verify every bank transaction was correctly matched to a resident.
2. As an administrator, I want to compare total bank credits against total payments created so that I can catch import discrepancies immediately.
3. As an administrator, I want to see which bank transactions remain unmatched after import processing so that I can manually review them.
4. As an administrator, I want to see unmatched debit transactions flagged for expense category assignment so that I can ensure accurate expense tracking.
5. As a financial secretary, I want to view a financial overview dashboard showing monthly revenue and expense trends so that I can monitor estate financial health.
6. As a financial secretary, I want to see collection health metrics (collection rate, invoice aging, overdue breakdown) so that I can prioritize collection efforts.
7. As a financial secretary, I want an invoice aging histogram showing exact days overdue so that I can identify the worst debtors at a glance.
8. As a financial secretary, I want to see portfolio value (bank balance + petty cash) on the dashboard so that I have a complete picture of estate finances.
9. As an administrator, I want to generate PDF reports for financial overview, collection, and invoice aging so that I can share them with stakeholders.
10. As an administrator, I want to generate PDF reports for debtors, indebtedness, development levy, and transaction logs so that I have reference documents for meetings.
11. As an administrator, I want to schedule reports to generate and email automatically on a daily, weekly, or monthly basis so that I don't need to manually generate routine reports.
12. As an administrator, I want scheduled reports stored in an archive accessible from the Reports page so that I can re-download previously generated reports.
13. As an administrator, I want to see version history for scheduled reports so that I can track what was sent and when.
14. As a chairman, I want the financial dashboard to replace the old analytics page so that the primary analytics surface is financial rather than search/miscellaneous metrics.

## Implementation Decisions

### Bank Reconciliation Summary
- Appears in the import results step, after processing completes (not a separate page).
- Displays a comparison table: bank credits total vs payments created, bank debits total vs expenses created, unmatched rows count.
- Unmatched rows are flagged with a direct link back to the review step for manual matching.
- Implementation hooks into the existing `processImport` results return structure. No new database tables required.

### Financial Dashboard
- Replaces the existing `/analytics` page entirely. Non-financial analytics (search, announcements) are deprecated.
- Dashboard sections: Revenue/Expense Trends (monthly bar/line chart), Collection Health (rate, aging brackets, top debtors), Invoice Aging (bracket summary cards + exact-day histogram), Portfolio Value card.
- Uses the existing recharts library (already installed and lazy-loaded in the analytics page-client pattern).
- Follows the existing analytics page-client pattern with `next/dynamic` lazy-loading and Suspense boundaries per section.

### Report PDF Generation
- Extends the existing report engine (`generateReport`) with a `format` parameter. When `format='pdf'`, the engine returns a PDF buffer alongside the structured data.
- PDF rendering uses `@react-pdf/renderer`, following the existing statement PDF pattern in `src/lib/pdf/account-statement.tsx`.
- Each report type has a dedicated PDF template component.
- Reports generated as PDFs are stored in a new `report_archive` table.

### Report Schedule Delivery
- Extends the existing `report-schedules.ts` to add a `processDueSchedules` function that finds schedules with `next_run_at <= now`, generates PDFs, emails recipients, archives the PDF, and updates `next_run_at`.
- Called by a new cron endpoint: `GET /api/cron/process-report-schedules`.
- Email delivery uses the existing Resend integration via `src/lib/email/send-email.ts`.
- Scheduled PDFs are stored in the `report_archive` table with `schedule_id` linking back to the schedule.

### Report Archive
- New `report_archive` table: `id`, `report_type`, `schedule_id` (nullable, null for on-demand generation), `generated_at`, `generated_by` (user who triggered), `recipients` (JSON array), `file_path` (storage bucket path), `file_size_bytes`, `format` (always 'pdf' initially).
- PDFs stored in a new Supabase storage bucket `report-pdfs` with RLS allowing read for users with `reports.view_financial` permission.
- Archive page accessible from the Reports page with re-download capability.

### Route Changes
- `/analytics` route now renders the new financial dashboard instead of the old analytics page.
- Old analytics components (search analytics, announcement analytics) are removed from the primary analytics route. Revenue trend charts used by the financial dashboard replace them.
- New `/api/cron/process-report-schedules` endpoint registered in `vercel.json`.

### Authorization
- Report generation, scheduling, and archive access require `REPORTS_VIEW_FINANCIAL` permission.
- Report schedule management requires `REPORTS_EXPORT` permission.
- PDF download from archive requires `REPORTS_VIEW_FINANCIAL` permission.
- All new server actions follow the `authorizePermission(PERMISSIONS.X)` + `logAudit()` contract.

## Testing Decisions

- Import reconciliation: unit test the reconciliation structure returned by the processing pipeline. Prior art: `process-email-import.test.ts`.
- Report engine PDF: integration test that calls `generateReport({ type, format: 'pdf' })` and asserts the returned buffer is a valid PDF containing expected data. Prior art: existing report engine in `report-engine.ts` (no existing tests, but the engine structure supports testing).
- Report schedule delivery: unit test `processDueSchedules` by mocking the email sender and storage uploader, asserting schedules are marked as executed. Prior art: `admin-notifier.test.ts`.
- Financial dashboard: component tests for each dashboard section rendering with mock data. Prior art: existing analytics tests pattern if they exist; otherwise standard component-level testing.
- Good tests verify external behavior (PDF structure contains expected content, not pixel-perfect rendering; schedule delivery sends to correct recipients; dashboard displays correct metric values).

## Out of Scope

- Legacy data import (135+ reviewed records) — deferred to a separate phase.
- WhatsApp delivery for scheduled reports — planned for future iteration, not this phase.
- Non-financial analytics (search analytics, announcement analytics) migration — these are deprecated from the analytics page but not migrated to new surfaces.
- Payment gateway integration — explicitly deferred per project roadmap.
- Invoice dispute system — existing disputes only log to audit; no new dispute table or workflow.
- SMS delivery — not operational, not part of this phase.

## Further Notes

- The existing analytics page-client already uses `next/dynamic` with `ssr: false` for recharts components. The new financial dashboard follows this same pattern for consistency.
- The report engine already supports 7 report types. Adding PDF rendering is an output-format extension, not a data-generation change.
- `@react-pdf/renderer` is already a dependency (used by the account statement PDF). No new package dependencies required.
- The existing Resend email integration handles sending; new report delivery code should use the same `sendEmail` function.

## Problem Statement

The current Generate Invoices action on `/billing` provides no preview before execution, no month/scope selection, no wallet/email controls, no resident-targeted billing profiles, and no robust duplicate/concurrency protection. Operators trigger invoice generation blindly against the current month without knowing what will be created, what wallets will be deducted, or what emails will be sent.

## Solution

A phased enhancement to the invoice generation pipeline adding:
1. Dry-run preview with target-month and scope selection
2. Explicit wallet/email side-effect controls
3. Resident-targeted billing profile support
4. Database-level duplicate/concurrency protection
5. Run history with downloadable results and retry support

## User Stories

1. As an administrator, I want to preview invoice generation before executing so that I can review what will be created before committing.
2. As a financial secretary, I want to choose the billing month and scope (house, street, resident) so that I can target specific billing runs.
3. As an administrator, I want to decide whether wallet deductions and emails fire during generation so that historical backfills don't trigger unintended notifications.
4. As an administrator, I want resident-targeted billing profiles to generate invoices against their configured roles so that individual resident charges are automated.
5. As an administrator, I want duplicate generation to be impossible so that re-running a period doesn't create duplicate invoices or wallet deductions.
6. As an administrator, I want failed runs to expose actionable details and be safely retryable so that I can recover from errors.
7. As a financial secretary, I want to see generation history with downloadable results so that I can audit billing operations.

## Implementation Decisions

- Preview uses the existing `generateMonthlyInvoices` engine but wraps it in a read-only mode: queries data, computes what would happen, returns structured preview without writing.
- Month selector and scope filters (house, street, resident) are passed as parameters to the preview and execution endpoints.
- Wallet debit and email delivery become boolean flags on the execution request, defaulting off for historical backfills.
- Resident-targeted profiles are processed in a separate pass that matches residents to profiles by applicable roles and validates overlap.
- Database uniqueness constraint on (resident_id, house_id, billing_profile_id, period_start, period_end) for invoices.
- `invoice_generation_log` table is already present and captures run metadata; it is extended with the new fields.

## Testing Decisions

- Preview: unit test that a dry-run returns expected invoice counts without writing.
- Execution: integration test that flags (wallet, email) are respected.
- Resident-targeted: unit test that role-matching produces correct resident assignments.
- Concurrency: integration test that duplicate runs are blocked.

## Out of Scope

- Payment gateway integration
- Legacy data import
- Statement generation (covered by separate PRD #24)

## What to build

Replace the admin dashboard’s duplicated card fanout with one permission-aware, typed snapshot read model that returns financial health, invoice distribution, security status, levy totals, quick stats, recent activity, and monthly trends through bounded Supabase aggregation. Wire the snapshot through the dashboard UI with explicit DTOs, stable query keys, loading/error behavior, and regression coverage.

## Acceptance criteria

## Problem Statement

The Personnel & Vendors directory lists active staff, contractors, vendors, and suppliers without showing who is accountable for each working relationship. Estate administrators cannot tell whether a person works for the Estate or for a particular Resident House, cannot see house-specific responsibility, and cannot preserve accountability history when work changes.

## Solution

Add dated Personnel Engagements. Each engagement makes either the Estate or a Resident House accountable for a Personnel record. Personnel can hold several concurrent engagements, but only one active engagement for each accountability target. Ending an engagement preserves history without changing the directory-wide Personnel status.

The Personnel directory surfaces compact active-accountability badges and filters. The existing Add/Edit Personnel dialog manages repeatable Estate and Resident-House engagements, including an optional context-specific responsibility and start/end dates.

## User Stories

1. As an estate administrator, I want to assign estate-employed Personnel to the Estate so that estate security, facilities, and administrative staff have a clear accountable party.
2. As an estate administrator, I want to assign Personnel to an active Resident House so that domestic staff, private drivers, gardeners, and house-specific contractors are traceable to the resident responsible for them.
3. As an estate administrator, I want to record an engagement-specific responsibility so that a person's general job title and their duty for a particular accountable party are distinguishable.
4. As an estate administrator, I want one Personnel record to have several active engagements so that shared workers and contractors can be accountable to several Resident Houses or to both the Estate and a Resident House.
5. As an estate administrator, I want the system to prevent duplicate active engagements for the same Personnel and accountability target so that accountability is unambiguous.
6. As an estate administrator, I want to create Resident-House Engagements only from active Resident Houses so that I cannot assign new responsibility to stale occupancy.
7. As an estate administrator, I want an ended Resident-House Engagement to remain visible after that Resident House becomes inactive so that the accountability history stays defensible.
8. As an estate administrator, I want to end one engagement without changing the Personnel status so that a person who continues working elsewhere remains Active.
9. As an estate administrator, I want existing Personnel with no engagement to show as Unassigned so that I can work through missing accountability data without the system making assumptions.
10. As an estate administrator, I want to filter the directory by Estate, Resident-House, and Unassigned accountability so that I can find the people for whom I am responsible.
11. As an estate administrator, I want the directory to show the first active accountability target and a count of additional targets so that I can scan the directory without losing multi-engagement context.
12. As an estate administrator, I want to open a Personnel record and see the full dated engagement history so that I can investigate responsibility during an incident or payment review.
13. As an estate administrator, I want to update the general Personnel job title without overwriting engagement-specific responsibility so that profile data remains reusable across engagements.
14. As an authorized administrator, I want all Personnel Engagement writes audited so that changes to estate and resident accountability are traceable.

## Implementation Decisions

- Add a Personnel Engagement persistence model linked to the existing Personnel-backed `vendors` table.
- An engagement has exactly one accountability scope: Estate or Resident House.
- A Resident-House Engagement references the existing Resident House relationship, rather than a House alone, because accountability must identify both the house and the responsible resident.
- The Estate scope has no Resident House reference. A Resident-House scope requires one.
- Every Personnel type can receive either engagement scope.
- The general Personnel `job_title` remains profile-level. An engagement may carry an optional engagement-specific responsibility.
- Engagements record a start date and optional end date. Ending an engagement preserves the record as history; it is never overwritten or deleted as a substitute for history.
- A new Resident-House Engagement is permitted only when its Resident House is active. Historical engagements remain readable even after that Resident House ends.
- Enforce one active engagement for the same Personnel and accountability target at the database level, alongside application validation.
- Personnel status remains directory-wide. An individual engagement ending does not make Personnel Inactive or Terminated.
- Existing Personnel receive no inferred engagement. They display as Unassigned until an administrator creates an engagement.
- Extend Personnel read models to include active engagement summaries and full engagement history for the editor.
- Extend the directory with an Accountability column and filter. An active Estate Engagement displays `Estate`; an active Resident-House Engagement displays the house and responsible resident; multiple targets display the first target plus an additional count.
- Extend the existing Add/Edit Personnel dialog with a repeatable Engagements section. It supports adding Estate and Resident-House engagements, responsibility, start/end dates, and ending an active engagement.
- New write actions use the existing Personnel management permission and audit integration convention.

## Testing Decisions

- Test externally visible behavior through Personnel engagement actions and the directory query model, not individual implementation helpers or table markup.
- Test valid Estate and Resident-House engagement creation, rejection of inactive Resident Houses, rejection of duplicate active targets, and preserved Personnel status/history after ending one engagement.
- Test directory query summaries and Estate, Resident-House, and Unassigned filter behavior.
- Add dialog behavior coverage for adding both scopes, validation feedback, and ending an existing engagement.
- Add the new write actions to the module-integration compliance coverage for permission checks and audit logging.

## Out of Scope

- A dedicated Personnel detail page.
- Personnel-to-Personnel or company/subcontractor accountability relationships.
- Inferring Estate responsibility for existing Personnel.
- Payroll, wage, contract, access-control, or expense-allocation workflows.
- Changing the general Personnel type or status lifecycle.

## Further Notes

- Canonical domain vocabulary is documented in `CONTEXT.md`: Personnel Engagement, Estate Engagement, Resident-House Engagement, Personnel Status, and Unassigned Personnel.
- This is an admin-dashboard feature. No Resident Portal work is included.

## Destination

Produce an implementation-ready, phased specification for the enterprise TOM Tracker: a Power Apps code app backed by SharePoint, piloted across the source tracker's Risk Management and Information Security units, then ready to become approved vertical-slice delivery issues.

## Notes

- Keep Wayfinder focused on decisions, evidence, and prerequisites—not implementation.
- Use `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling` for decision tickets.
- **`CMB Corporate Strategy 2026 21082026.xlsx` is the source of truth.** Where it and an earlier assumption disagree, the tracker wins — including for the pilot definition.
- The product baseline is [`prd.md`](../blob/main/prd.md), **version 0.4**, revised 2026-08-25 to match the tracker.
- The application is a Power Apps code app using SharePoint Lists; Power BI remains a separate reporting experience.
- Deploy the Power Apps code app to **Power Code Apps - Dev** (`e203e4b3-24aa-e1a9-8ac9-dd987e006344`). Deploy Power Automate flows to **Coronation Merchant Bank** (`d84a9014-710d-4a9d-8901-c26a4d2f2467`).
- End users have Power Apps Premium licences. Code Apps must be enabled in the Code Apps Dev environment, and GitHub is the code source of truth.
- Use a dedicated SharePoint site, a normalized multi-list model, a controlled document library for evidence, and append-only Activity History.
- Security must be enforced at the SharePoint data layer as well as the application layer. Application roles and organizational scopes are explicit managed records.
- Retention is out of scope for the pilot and is a production-readiness gate.
- Pilot authorization uses a SharePoint **Role Assignment** list with one row per user, role, and organizational scope. Entra group provisioning/integration is deferred until after the code app is confirmed working.

## Decisions so far

### Domain model — set by PRD 0.4 from the source tracker

- TOM hierarchy is **TOM → Strategy → Milestone → Activity**.
- **Strategy** = the tracker's Initiative (44), keyed by a unique **Strategy Code** from `Initiative ID`.
- **Milestone** (128) is a governed, **non-workflow-bearing** level. No owner, reviewer, approver or SLA; status and dates derived from its Activities. Workflow configuration stays at Application, Strategy and Activity level.
- **Activity** = the tracker's Task (350).
- **Strategic Lever is an organizational unit, not a TOM level** — 16 units, each with a code prefix already used in `Initiative ID`, each with an effectively disjoint owner set.
- Organizational unit and Primary Responsibility/Owner are recorded on the **Strategy** and inherited by Activities, overridable at Activity level with audit.
- Multi-person source ownership resolves to one Primary Owner, an optional Senior Owner, and Consulted stakeholders. Unresolvable names block migration of their Strategy.
- Controlled statuses include **Deprioritized** (distinct from Cancelled) and **On Hold**. Overdue stays a calculated condition.
- Delivery month and quarter are **derived**, never stored.
- Activities completed before go-live are flagged **migrated-complete**, and carry the **full §9.1 attribute set** — historical Activities are not exempted from attribute completeness.

### Organizational model

- The 16 units are **peers**. None nests inside another, and the application shall not infer nesting.
- **The Division is derived from people, not from an org chart.** When a Primary Responsibility/Owner is created, that person's **Divisional Head** is captured alongside them. Units whose Owners share a Divisional Head belong to the same Division.
- **The Divisional Head defines the RBAC scope boundary** above unit level.
- Pilot organizational hierarchy is **Enterprise → Division (derived) → Department/Unit (the 16 units)**. Group and Team are unused but not designed out.
- Sub-units that exist only inside Strategy titles — Credit Risk, Market Risk, Enterprise Risk Management, Operational Risk, Sustainability — are **not** created as organizational nodes. Where such a distinction needs tracking it is expressed as Strategies and Activities under the owning unit.

### Pilot — rewritten from the tracker

The earlier definition of "one Division with six sub-units" is superseded. Risk Management and Information Security are **sibling units** in the source, with separate code prefixes and separate owners, and the pilot is defined that way.

| Unit | Code | Strategies | Milestones | Activities | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Risk Management | `RM` | 7 | 7 | 36 | Saheed Alamutu |
| Information Security | `IS` / `ISO` | 5 | 14 | 51 | Feyijimi Adewole |
| **Pilot total** | | **12** | **21** | **87** | |

Status split across the 87: Completed 70, In-Progress 13, Yet to Start 4.

- TOM Administrator: **Feyijimi Adewole** (`fadewole@coronationmb.com`).
- Sponsor: **Chima Ekwonwa** (`cekwonwa@coronationmb.com`).
- Divisional placement of both units follows from the Divisional Heads captured for their two Owners.
- The pilot user population is **determined by the onboarding capture** (#14) — Owners, Divisional Heads, assignees, reviewers, approvers and stakeholders — not assumed in advance. The tracker names only the two Owners.
- Pilot success still requires working workflow, RBAC, audit history, reporting, performance, and UAT acceptance evidence.
- One migration note specific to the pilot: **`RM08` is bound to two different Strategies across both units** — "Risk Management Operational Enhancement" (4 Activities, Risk Management) and "Operational Resilience for Digital Channels" (9 Activities, Information Security). It must be re-coded before migration.

## Open sequence

**#12 / #14 → #7 → #6 → #5 → #8 → #9 → #10**, with #4 reduced to the post-pilot authoritative-source question.

## Not yet specified

- The authoritative enterprise hierarchy source for the post-pilot period, and its synchronization design (#4).
- The controlled Activity Category values (#14).
- Detailed Opportunity lifecycle after the core record and workflow model is settled. The tracker holds no Opportunity data, so this carries no migration dependency.
- Exact SLA values, reminder cadence, escalation thresholds, and delegated-action policy.
- Production records-retention policy and evidence retention rules.
- Final CI/CD and release-approval implementation after code-app prerequisites are validated.
- Post-pilot Entra group integration/provisioning, including directory group design and synchronization ownership.

## Out of scope

- Mobile- and tablet-specific experiences for the initial release.
- Full project-management, financial-management, resource-capacity, or timesheet features.
- Dataverse migration unless the licensing decision changes.

## Question

How do the four levels in the Corporate Strategy tracker (**Strategic Lever → Initiative → Milestone → Task**) map onto the confirmed TOM hierarchy (**TOM → Strategy → Activity**), and is *Strategic Lever* a Strategy level, an Activity Category, or an organizational dimension?

## Why this is now open

`CMB Corporate Strategy 2026 21082026.xlsx` (350 data rows, sheet `Corporate Strategy`) is the real-world shape of the work the TOM Tracker must hold. It carries four nested levels, not two:

- **Strategic Lever** — 19 raw values, ~16 after normalizing spelling variants.
- **Initiative** (`Initiative Name` + `Initiative ID`) — 44 groups.
- **Milestone** — 128 distinct.
- **Task** — 350 rows.

PRD §3.7, §5.2 and §5.6 assert a fixed two-level TOM structure. Three of the four tracker levels have no home in it.

## Evidence

Strategic Lever distribution (raw):

| Lever | Rows |
| --- | --- |
| Customer Experience | 79 |
| Information Security | 49 (+2 as `Information Security ` with trailing space) |
| Risk Management | 36 |
| Admin & Facility Management | 32 |
| Global Markets & Treasury | 23 (+4 as `Global Markets and Treasury`) |
| Corporate Banking | 22 |
| FI | 19 (+2 as `Financial Institutions`) |
| Abuja Business | 18 |
| Marketing & Communications | 16 |
| Technology | 10 |
| FINCON | 9 |
| Investment Banking | 8 |
| Public Sector | 7 |
| Private Banking | 6 |
| Affluent Banking | 5 |
| Talent | 3 |

Several lever values (`FINCON`, `Technology`, `Talent`, `Abuja Business`, `Public Sector`) read as **organizational functions**, not strategic directions — so Lever may be carrying organizational meaning that PRD §5.6 requires to stay in a separate structure.

## Options to decide between

1. **Strategy = Initiative.** Lever becomes Activity Category (or a Strategy attribute); Milestone becomes an Activity grouping attribute; Task = Activity. Keeps the two-level hierarchy intact; loses milestone-level roll-up and review.
2. **Recursive Strategy.** Lever = parent Strategy, Initiative = child Strategy, Milestone = Activity, Task = sub-Activity. Fits the data; changes the PRD's fixed depth, and forces a decision on Activity nesting, completion roll-up and workflow aggregation.
3. **Strategy = Lever, Activity = Task**, with Initiative and Milestone as governed attributes on the Activity. Simplest to build; flattens two levels the business currently manages by.

## Decide

- The chosen mapping, level by level.
- Whether *Strategic Lever* is a Strategy level, an Activity Category, or an organizational node.
- Whether Milestone needs its own completion, review, or reporting roll-up.
- Whether Activity nesting (Task under Milestone) is in or out of pilot scope.

## Blocks

Blocks #6 (lifecycle, aggregation and completion semantics), #7 (list and relationship model), and #9 (semantic model grain).

## Task

Deliver the Opportunity capability, now specified in **PRD 0.5 §10.3–10.7**. This closes the last open feature gap in the product.

## Lifecycle

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Identified** | Raised by any authorized user; minimal data |
| **Under Assessment** | Owner evaluates value, effort and fit |
| **Awaiting Decision** | Approver decides |
| **Approved** | Accepted, awaiting conversion |
| **Converted** | Realized as a Strategy or Activities — terminal |
| **Rejected** | Not proceeding, rationale recorded |
| **Deferred** | Valid but not now; returns to Under Assessment on its review date |

## Deliberately lighter than the Activity path

Opportunity approval is **single-stage**. No reviewer pools, no sequential or parallel review, no rework cycles, no second approval level. An Opportunity is a proposal, not governed delivery work — putting it through §11 would make raising an idea as heavy as delivering one.

## Conversion

On conversion the application creates either a new Strategy or Activities under a nominated Strategy, carries across title, description, unit, Owner, stakeholders and evidence, and records a **permanent bidirectional link**. The Opportunity is retained read-only and stays reportable: it is the record of *why* a Strategy or Activity exists, and that provenance survives delivery.

## Sequencing

The source baseline contains **no Opportunity data**, so this is greenfield with no migration dependency. It can be delivered after the core Strategy → Milestone → Activity model without blocking the pilot, and should be — the pilot's value is in governing work that already exists.

## Done when

The lifecycle, single-stage approval, conversion with bidirectional linkage, the notification set in §10.6, and Opportunity reporting are implemented and demonstrated.

## Summary

Seven admin routes are not registered in the middleware's route table, so they receive **no authentication and no permission check**. An unauthenticated visitor can load them and gets the full admin dashboard shell.

Found during manual QA pass `QAT-AUTH-10`. Full report: `docs/qat/reports/qat-auth-20260829.md`.

## Affected routes

`/documents`, `/announcements`, `/personnel`, `/projects`, `/expenditure`, `/analytics`, `/notifications`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a browser with no Residio session (or clear cookies).
2. Navigate to `http://localhost:3000/documents`.

## Expected

Redirect to `/login?next=%2Fdocuments`, the same as every other admin route. Verified working for 18 routes including `/residents`, `/houses`, `/payments`, `/billing`, `/security`, `/reports`, `/approvals`, `/settings/**`, `/payments/email-imports`, `/portal`.

## Actual

HTTP 200 at the requested path. The page renders the admin shell with the complete sidebar IA (Residents, Houses, Transactions, Invoices & Dues, Security, Reports, Approvals, Settings, System...). `/personnel` additionally renders the directory table header. Reproduced on all seven routes.

## Data exposure

No resident or estate data was returned to the unauthenticated session — stat cards read `0` and tables showed empty states. RLS is holding at the data layer. This is currently **structural** exposure (admin IA, module names, page chrome), not a data breach.

## Why this is High rather than Medium

The same missing configuration governs *authenticated but under-privileged* users, and both gates that would stop them are absent for these paths:

- `routePermissionConfig` (`src/middleware.ts:8`) omits all seven → no permission check runs.
- `adminOnlyRoutes` (`src/middleware.ts:25`) omits all seven → the resident-blocking rule does not apply either.

For two of them this is a straightforward wiring omission — `src/lib/auth/action-roles.ts:181` already declares them:

```ts
'/documents': [PERMISSIONS.DOCUMENTS_VIEW],
'/announcements': [PERMISSIONS.ANNOUNCEMENTS_VIEW],
```

but the middleware keeps a hand-maintained second copy of that table which never picked them up. `/personnel`, `/projects`, `/expenditure`, `/analytics` and `/notifications` appear in **neither** table, so they were never gated at all.

Whether a `resident`-role account can read data on these pages depends entirely on per-table RLS. Cross-role testing was out of scope for this pass, so that risk is unquantified.

## Suggested fix

`src/middleware.ts:8-28` — derive `routePermissionConfig` from `ROUTE_PERMISSIONS` rather than maintaining a parallel copy that can silently drift, and add the five ungated routes to both `ROUTE_PERMISSIONS` and `adminOnlyRoutes`.

## Environment

Build `43579eb` (master), Next.js dev server, cloud Supabase.

Found during manual QA pass `QAT-PAY-06`. Full report: `docs/qat/reports/qat-payments-20260829.md`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in as `super_admin`.
2. Navigate to `/payments/new` (or click "Record Payment" from `/payments`, or the "Record Payment" quick action on `/dashboard`).

## Expected

The Record Payment form renders with resident/house selector, amount, method, status, date and reference fields.

## Actual

```
Something went wrong
Functions cannot be passed directly to Client Components unless you explicitly expose it
by marking it with "use server". Or maybe you meant to call this function rather than return it.
  {$$typeof: ..., render: function CreditCard}
                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
Error ID: 3256909499
Try again   Dashboard
```

Console:

```
Only plain objects can be passed to Client Components from Server Components.
Classes or other objects with methods are not supported.
  <... title=... description=... icon={{$$typeof: ..., render: ...}}>
                                      ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
The above error occurred in the <EnhancedPageHeader> component.
```

## Root cause

`src/app/(dashboard)/payments/new/page.tsx` is an **async Server Component**:

```tsx
export default async function NewPaymentPage({ searchParams }: {...}) {
    ...
    <EnhancedPageHeader
        title="Record Payment"
        description="Enter payment details for a resident."
        icon={CreditCard}          // <- lucide component passed across the RSC boundary
    />
```

`EnhancedPageHeader` lives in `src/components/dashboard/enhanced-stat-card.tsx`, which is `'use client'`. A lucide icon is a `forwardRef` object containing a `render` function, so React cannot serialize it from a Server Component to a Client Component.

This is an isolated regression, not a systemic pattern. Every other page that passes `icon=` to `EnhancedPageHeader` is itself a Client Component:

```

src/app/(dashboard)/announcements/page.tsx                 'use client'
src/app/(dashboard)/billing/page.tsx                       'use client'
src/app/(dashboard)/billing/generate/page.tsx              'use client'
src/app/(dashboard)/documents/page.tsx                     'use client'
src/app/(dashboard)/houses/page.tsx                        'use client'
src/app/(dashboard)/houses/new/page.tsx                    'use client'
src/app/(dashboard)/notifications/page.tsx                 'use client'
src/app/(dashboard)/payments/page.tsx                      'use client'
src/app/(dashboard)/personnel/page.tsx                     'use client'
src/app/(dashboard)/residents/page.tsx                     'use client'
src/app/(dashboard)/residents/new/page.tsx                 'use client'
src/app/(dashboard)/security/page.tsx                      'use client'
src/app/(dashboard)/security/contacts/page.tsx             'use client'
src/app/(dashboard)/payments/new/page.tsx                  <-- NOT a client component
```

`/payments/new` is the only one of the fifteen that is a Server Component.

The primary path for recording a resident payment is unusable. Whether payments can still be entered through the bulk payment sheet on `/payments` was not verified in this pass, so a workaround may or may not exist.

Note this page needs to stay a Server Component to `await searchParams`, so the fix is likely to keep the server page and move the header (or the icon prop) behind a client boundary, rather than adding `'use client'` to the page.

## Summary

`/settings/system` and `/settings/system/health` both crash to the error boundary with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'overall')`, thrown from `<CronHealthCard>`.

Found during manual QA pass `QAT-SMK-19` / `QAT-SMK-20`. Full report: `docs/qat/reports/qat-smoke-20260829.md`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in as `super_admin`.
2. Navigate to `/settings/system`.
3. Wait for load. Repeat for `/settings/system/health`.

Reproduced in a clean browser tab with a 20-second settle wait, on both routes.

## Expected

The System settings hub renders, including the cron job health card.

## Actual

```
Something went wrong
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'overall')
Try again   Dashboard
```

Console:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'overall')
The above error occurred in the <CronHealthCard> component.
It was handled by the <ErrorBoundaryHandler> error boundary.
```

## Root cause

`src/components/dashboard/cron-health-card.tsx:152`

```ts
const overallStatus = data?.status || (data as { overall?: string }).overall || 'unknown';
const jobs = data?.jobs || [];
const lastChecked = data?.lastChecked || (data as { timestamp?: string }).timestamp;
```

The first term uses optional chaining and correctly yields `undefined` when the React Query result has no data. The **second term does not** — `(data as {...}).overall` dereferences `data` directly and throws as soon as `data` is `undefined`. The `|| 'unknown'` fallback is unreachable.

Line 154 repeats the same unguarded pattern for `.timestamp`.

The component already gets this right in its parsing path — line 45 guards with `if (data && (data.status || data.overall) && Array.isArray(data.jobs))`. Only the render path at 152/154 is missing the guard.

`data` ends up undefined when `/api/health/cron-status` fails or returns an empty payload. That route uses `createAdminClient()` and queries `invoice_generation_log` and related tables. The component has loading and error branches above line 152, so this is specifically the "query resolved but payload absent" case.

## Impact

Two admin pages are entirely unreachable. Notably, `/settings/system/health` is the page an administrator would use to notice that cron jobs have stopped running — so this defect disables exactly the monitoring surface that would surface a related outage.

Add optional chaining to both fallback terms:

```ts
const overallStatus = data?.status || (data as { overall?: string } | undefined)?.overall || 'unknown';
const lastChecked = data?.lastChecked || (data as { timestamp?: string } | undefined)?.timestamp;
```

Worth also checking why the health endpoint returns an empty payload in this environment, since the crash is masking whatever that underlying condition is.

## Summary

`approveAsOccupier` marks an approval request as `approved` but never applies the change the request was raised for. The requester sees a success toast and the request moves to Approved, while the underlying record keeps its old value. This is a silent data-integrity bug: the audit trail and the approvals queue both claim a change was accepted that never happened.

## Evidence

`src/actions/approvals/developer-owner-approvals.ts` — `approveAsOccupier` validates the approver, updates the request row, and returns success. The apply step is an unimplemented TODO:

```ts
// TODO: Apply the approved changes (would need to know the action type)
// This would typically be handled by the calling code after approval
```

The caller does not apply it either — `src/hooks/use-approvals.ts:157` (`useApproveAsOccupier`) only invalidates React Query caches on success.

By contrast the **admin** path is correct: `approveRequest` in `src/actions/approvals/index.ts:203` calls `applyRequestedChanges(request)` before flipping the status, and bails if that fails.

## Why it matters for the pilot

Approvals gate two financial surfaces:

- **Billing profile effective-date changes** — `updateBillingProfile` (`src/actions/billing/profiles.ts`) routes through `createApprovalRequest` when the change would affect already-issued invoices and the actor cannot auto-approve.
- **Estate bank account edits** — `src/actions/imports/bank-accounts.ts`.

In both cases an occupier approval currently produces an approved-but-unapplied request, and the operator has no signal that the change did not land.

## Proposed approach

Route `approveAsOccupier` through the same apply path the admin flow already uses, rather than reimplementing it:

1. Extract/reuse `applyRequestedChanges` from `src/actions/approvals/index.ts` so both approve paths share one implementation.
2. Call it **before** setting `status = 'approved'`, and return the failure without mutating status when it fails — mirroring `approveRequest`'s ordering.
3. Keep the existing `logAudit` call (added in `93ed5d0`), and extend its metadata to record whether the change was applied.
4. If a request type genuinely has no apply handler, fail closed with an explicit error rather than reporting success.

### Alternative (pilot stopgap)

If this cannot land before the controlled pilot, disable the occupier approve action in the UI so only the admin path (which applies correctly) can approve. That is a smaller change and removes the silent-failure surface.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Approving as occupier applies the requested change to the target record, verified for both `billing_profile_effective_date` and the estate bank account request type.
- [ ] When the apply step fails, the request stays `pending`, the caller receives the error, and no audit entry claims approval.
- [ ] `approveAsOccupier` and `approveRequest` share a single apply implementation — no duplicated per-type logic.
- [ ] A request type with no registered apply handler returns an explicit error instead of a success result.
- [ ] The audit entry records the applied outcome.
- [ ] Regression test covering: successful apply, failed apply leaves status `pending`, and unhandled request type fails closed.
- [ ] `npm test`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, and `npm run build` all pass.

## Out of scope

- The **Security module** (`src/actions/security/**`), `/security/verify`, access codes, visitor/vehicle records and the access-verification flow — all already carry permission checks and are not part of this work.
- The external barrier/access-verification API (`/api/v1/access/verify`) — separately out of scope.
- The permission gaps tracked in the companion RBAC issue.
- Resident Portal / self-service surfaces, per the standing admin-dashboard-first direction.

## References

- Identified during the controlled-pilot readiness review, 2026-08-29.
- Audit logging for this action was added in `93ed5d0` on `fix/build-and-audit-coverage`; the apply gap was deliberately left untouched there.

## Summary

25 admin-facing write actions authenticate the caller (`supabase.auth.getUser()`) but never check **which role** is acting. Server actions are directly invocable by any authenticated session, so for these files RLS is the only authorization boundary — the application layer has no second line and no role-appropriate error.

The sharpest case is **`src/actions/billing/profiles.ts`**, which has no check at all — not even `getUser()`. `createBillingProfile`, `updateBillingProfile`, `deleteBillingProfile` and `duplicateBillingProfile` go straight from Zod validation to the database. These define the rate card that determines what every resident is charged.

## Severity

**Not an open hole today.** These actions use the user-scoped server client, and RLS restricts the underlying tables — e.g.:

```sql
CREATE POLICY "Admins chairmen fin sec can manage billing profiles"
  ON public.billing_profiles FOR ALL
  USING (public.get_my_role() IN ('admin','chairman','financial_secretary'));
```

The database is enforcing what the application skipped. The risk is defence-in-depth: any table whose RLS is later relaxed, or any action switched to `createAdminClient()`, loses its only guard silently. It also violates the mandatory contract in `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` that every write action calls `authorizePermission` first.

## In scope — 25 files

All target permission constants **already exist** in `src/lib/auth/action-roles.ts`. No new constants, no `permission_category` enum migration, and no permission-seeding migration are required.

| File | Suggested permission |
| --- | --- |
| `billing/profiles.ts` (no check at all) | `BILLING_MANAGE_PROFILES` |
| `approvals/developer-owner-approvals.ts` | `APPROVALS_APPROVE_REJECT` |
| `documents/categories.ts` | `DOCUMENTS_MANAGE_CATEGORIES` |
| `imports/bank-accounts.ts` | `IMPORTS_CREATE` / `IMPORTS_REVIEW` |
| `imports/create-import.ts` | `IMPORTS_CREATE` |
| `imports/process-import.ts` | `IMPORTS_REVIEW` |
| `imports/match-residents.ts` | `IMPORTS_REVIEW` |
| `notifications/schedules.ts` | `NOTIFICATIONS_MANAGE` |
| `notifications/templates.ts` | `NOTIFICATIONS_MANAGE` |
| `reference/create-street.ts` | `SETTINGS_MANAGE_REFERENCE` |
| `reference/create-house-type.ts` | `SETTINGS_MANAGE_REFERENCE` |
| `reference/duplicate-street.ts` | `SETTINGS_MANAGE_REFERENCE` |
| `reference/transaction-tags.ts` | `SETTINGS_MANAGE_REFERENCE` |
| `reports/report-schedules.ts` | `REPORT_SUBSCRIPTIONS_MANAGE` |
| `residents/aliases.ts` | `RESIDENTS_UPDATE` |
| `residents/inherit-domestic-staff.ts` | `HOUSES_ASSIGN_RESIDENT` |
| `residents/move-out-landlord.ts` | `HOUSES_ASSIGN_RESIDENT` |
| `residents/remove-ownership.ts` | `HOUSES_ASSIGN_RESIDENT` |
| `residents/sponsor-cascade.ts` | `HOUSES_ASSIGN_RESIDENT` |
| `residents/swap-resident-roles.ts` | `HOUSES_ASSIGN_RESIDENT` |
| `residents/update-resident-house.ts` | `HOUSES_ASSIGN_RESIDENT` |
| `settings/backfill-ownership-history.ts` | `SYSTEM_MANAGE_DATA_RETENTION` |
| `settings/hierarchical-settings.ts` | `SETTINGS_MANAGE_GENERAL` |
| `settings/upload-estate-logo.ts` | `SETTINGS_MANAGE_GENERAL` |
| `verification/send-verification.ts` | `RESIDENTS_VERIFY` |

The mapping is a starting point — confirm each against `ROUTE_PERMISSIONS` and the role matrix rather than applying blindly. Where an action is reachable by a non-admin acting on their own record, prefer `authorizeAnyPermission` or an explicit ownership branch over widening the permission.

## Out of scope

- **Security module** — `src/actions/security/**` (contacts, codes, categories, settings, access logs, vehicles, visitor analytics), `/security/verify`, and code verification. Verified already compliant: every file in that module carries `authorizePermission` / `hasSecurityPermission` checks. Do not modify.
- **External access-verification API** (`/api/v1/access/verify`, API keys, rate limiting) — not built, and not part of this work.
- **The 17 actions exempt by design**, already documented in `PERMISSION_ALLOWLIST` with per-entry reasons: resident self-service and ownership-authorized flows (`payments/submit-payment-proof`, `billing/pay-*-with-wallet`, `paystack/*`), the signature-verified Paystack webhook, `CRON_SECRET`-driven jobs (`email-imports/*`, `reports/process-schedules`, `analytics/refresh-payment-cadence-summary`), pre-auth flows (`auth/register-resident-portal`, `two-factor/verify`), business-rule authorization (`residents/add-household-member`), and reads whose only write is their own access log (`documents/download-document`, `announcements/read-receipts`). **Do not add `authorizePermission` to these.**
- **Audit logging** — completed separately in `93ed5d0`; write actions missing `logAudit` went from 28 to 5.
- **Resident Portal / self-service**, per the standing admin-dashboard-first direction.

## Success criteria

- [ ] All 25 files call an authorization helper before their first write, returning the standard `{ error }` shape on failure.
- [ ] `billing/profiles.ts` additionally gains an authentication check; all four exported write functions are covered.
- [ ] No new permission constants, enum migrations, or seeding migrations were needed (confirm; if one proves necessary, follow the migration pattern in `CLAUDE.md`).
- [ ] Each of the 25 entries is **removed** from `PERMISSION_ALLOWLIST` in `src/__tests__/integration/module-integration.test.ts`; the 17 by-design entries stay, with their comments intact.
- [ ] The suite's gap summary drops from **42 permission gaps to 17**.
- [ ] Tests assert the unauthorized path for at least `billing/profiles.ts`, one `residents/*` lifecycle action, and one `imports/*` action.
- [ ] No behaviour change for a correctly-permissioned admin: existing flows still succeed end to end.
- [ ] `npm test`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint` (no new errors), and `npm run build` all pass.

## Suggested sequencing

Land in small per-module commits rather than one sweep, so a regression is easy to bisect: `billing/profiles` first (highest value), then `residents/*`, `settings/*`, `reference/*`, `imports/*`, then the remainder.

## References

- Identified during the controlled-pilot readiness review, 2026-08-29.
- Allowlists were corrected in `93ed5d0`: 21 of 72 permission entries had been suppressing files that already complied, so the pre-existing counts understated real coverage.
- Contract: `AGENTS.md` "Server actions — MANDATORY integration"; `CLAUDE.md` "Module Integration Requirements".

## Summary

Every house detail page reports **"Financial Status: Clear — No pending payments"** and **"Last Inspection: 2025-12-01 — Compliance verified"** regardless of the property's actual state. Both values are hardcoded.

Found during manual QA pass `QAT-HSE-11`. Full report: `docs/qat/reports/qat-houses-20260829.md`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in as `super_admin`.
2. Open `/billing` and note that resident **FEYIJIMI ADEWOLE** at **18A, Kayode Oni Animashaun** has multiple unpaid Service Charge invoices (₦10,000 each; Jan, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug 2026 all showing `unpaid`, several past their due date).
3. Navigate to that house's detail page: `/houses/f866af4d-4f58-48fc-826e-df7684bdaa83`.
4. Read the Overview tab.

## Expected

The Financial Status card reflects the property's real outstanding balance.

## Actual

```
18A  Kayode Oni Animashaun  Duplex
Occupancy        Occupied — 1 active residents
Financial Status Clear — No pending payments        <-- FALSE
Last Inspection  2025-12-01 — Compliance verified   <-- hardcoded
```

The same "Last Inspection 2025-12-01 / Compliance verified" also appears on a house created minutes earlier during this test run (`QAT-01`, id `a6a5f7df-9cfb-485e-8219-d1d00084d4c9`) — a property that has never been inspected.

## Root cause

`src/app/(dashboard)/houses/[id]/page.tsx:596-601`

```tsx
<HouseStatsCards
  occupancyStatus={house.is_occupied ? 'occupied' : 'vacant'}
  totalResidents={activeResidents.length}
  pendingDues={0} // Mocked for now, pending backend integration
  lastInspectionDate="2025-12-01"
/>
```

`pendingDues` is hardcoded to `0` and `lastInspectionDate` to the string literal `"2025-12-01"`. The receiving component renders them as real figures (`src/components/houses/house-stats-cards.tsx:72`), with the static caption "Compliance verified" beneath the date.

Note the first two props on the same call ARE wired to real data, which is what makes the other two read as genuine rather than obviously placeholder.

## Impact

An administrator opening a property page is told it is financially clear when it owes money. There is no visual cue that the value is a placeholder — it sits beside two correctly-wired cards in identical styling.

The realistic failure is an operational decision made on false information: granting access, issuing a clearance, or skipping a debt follow-up because the property page said "Clear". The move-out flow explicitly depends on financial clearance, so a mocked zero on the property view is pointed in a risky direction.

The inspection date is lower-stakes but asserts compliance about all 179 properties, including ones created seconds ago.

## Suggested fix

Wire `pendingDues` to the same source `/billing` uses for this house (there is already a `getHousePaymentStatus` action), and either wire the inspection date to real data or remove the card until an inspection feature exists. If either has to stay mocked in the interim, it should be visibly labelled as such rather than rendered as fact.

## Environment

Build `43579eb` (master), Next.js dev server, cloud Supabase.

Found during manual QA pass `QAT-BIL-D1`. Report: `docs/qat/reports/qat-billing-20260829.md` on branch `qa/manual-qat-20260829`.

## Summary

The invoice status donut on `/dashboard` and `/analytics` sums five buckets that are not mutually exclusive, so overdue invoices are counted twice and every segment is drawn against an inflated denominator.

## Evidence

Displayed: Paid 570, Unpaid 19, Partially Paid 0, Overdue 18, Void 0 — summing to **607**.
True invoice count is **589**, confirmed independently by `/billing`, which runs an unfiltered `count: 'exact'` over the table. The gap is exactly the 18 overdue rows.

## Root cause

`overdue` is not a stored status. It is derived — `src/actions/dashboard/get-enhanced-dashboard-stats.ts:447`:

```ts
supabase.from('invoices').select('*', { count: 'exact', head: true })
  .in('status', ['unpaid', 'partially_paid'])
  .lt('due_date', new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]),
```

`fetchInvoiceDistribution` runs five count queries and does not exclude the overdue subset from the `unpaid` bucket, so the same rows appear in both. The card then treats the five as a partition — `src/components/dashboard/invoice-distribution-card.tsx:33` (inside `DonutChart`) and again at line 178:

```ts
const total = Object.values(distribution).reduce((sum, val) => sum + val, 0);
```

## Impact

Paid renders as 570/607 = 93.9% of the ring when it is really 570/589 = 96.8%. The Overdue wedge is drawn as its own slice while those invoices already sit inside the Unpaid wedge — the chart shows parts that do not form a whole.

Each individual figure is correct in isolation; the defect is charting a subset alongside its own superset.

## Suggested fix

Either exclude overdue from the unpaid bucket before charting, or render overdue as an annotation rather than a segment.

Build `43579eb`.

Found during manual QA pass `QAT-SEC-D1`. Report: `docs/qat/reports/qat-security-20260829.md` on branch `qa/manual-qat-20260829`.

## Summary

The Nigerian phone format rule for security contacts is written but never attached to any field. Only a length check runs, so malformed and foreign numbers create live gate-access contacts.

## Steps to reproduce

Submit the Register Security Contact form (`/security/contacts/new`) with each phone value:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `12345` | Rejected — "Phone number must be at least 10 digits" |
| `+1234567890` | **Accepted** — contact created |
| `0912345678` | **Accepted** — contact created |

Both accepted values violate the documented format (`+1234567890` is not a Nigerian number; `0912345678` has an invalid third digit and is a digit short).

## Root cause

`src/lib/validators/security-contact.ts:15` declares the rule:

```ts
const phoneRegex = /^(\+234|0)[789][01]\d{8}$/;
```

`src/lib/validators/security-contact.ts:36` — the field it should govern — never applies it:

```ts
phone_primary: z.string().min(10, 'Phone number must be at least 10 digits'),
```

`phoneRegex` is referenced **exactly once in the whole codebase: its own declaration.** It is dead code.

The resolver itself is wired correctly (`src/components/security/security-contact-form.tsx:69` uses `zodResolver(createSecurityContactSchema)`), so the constraint simply was never attached to the field.

## Impact

Security contacts are the people issued gate access codes. The phone number is how a guard reaches a visitor or calls the resident to confirm entry, so unreachable numbers degrade exactly that check. This permits bad data rather than granting unauthorised access — but it is on the access-control surface, and the intended rule is already written and one line from working.

`phone_secondary` and `next_of_kin_phone` are `z.string().optional()` with no format or length constraint at all, which is worth considering in the same change.

Build `43579eb`.

Found during manual QA pass `QAT-XC-D1`. Report: `docs/qat/reports/qat-cross-cutting-20260829.md` on branch `qa/manual-qat-20260829`.

## Summary

When the client-side RBAC permission fetch times out, the resulting empty-permission profile is cached for 5 minutes, silently removing every permission-gated control from the UI with no message to the user.

## Observed

This appeared in the console during ordinary admin navigation — not provoked, not under load:

```
[AuthProvider] RBAC fetch failed or timed out: {message: "RBAC fetch timeout"}
```

## It fails closed — this is not a security hole

Worth stating up front. On timeout `permissions` keeps its initial value (`src/lib/auth/auth-provider.tsx:285`):

```ts
let permissions: string[] = [];
```

and every check consults only that array (`auth-provider.tsx:382`):

```ts
const hasPermission = useCallback((permission: string): boolean => {
  return profile?.permissions?.includes(permission) ?? false;
}, [profile?.permissions]);
```

`[].includes(x)` is false for all `x`, so gated UI is hidden rather than shown. No super-admin bypass or default-allow path exists in `src/lib/auth/`. Server-side `authorizePermission()` re-queries the database independently on every call and does not read client state.

## The actual defect

The timeout is swallowed (`auth-provider.tsx:333`):

```ts
} catch (err) {
  console.error('[AuthProvider] RBAC fetch failed or timed out:', err);
}
```

Execution falls through and the degraded profile is committed and cached unconditionally (`auth-provider.tsx:352`):

```ts
setProfile(newProfile);
setCachedProfile(newProfile);
```

`setCachedProfile` writes to `sessionStorage` under `residio_profile_cache` with a **5-minute TTL** (`auth-provider.tsx:45-70`), and `getCachedProfile()` serves it back until it expires.

## Impact

One database query exceeding 15 seconds leaves a super_admin with no permission-gated controls anywhere in the app for up to five minutes, persisting across navigations. Confirmed examples of what disappears:

- "Correction" button and invoice-correction dialog — `src/app/(dashboard)/billing/[id]/page.tsx:127`
- "View as Resident" impersonation link — `src/components/dashboard/sidebar.tsx:340`
- Document upload / edit / delete controls — `src/app/(dashboard)/documents/page.tsx:28`

The user is told nothing. No toast, no banner, no retry — only a `console.error` no administrator will see. The application simply stops offering functions it offered a moment ago.

## Two separable problems

1. **Caching a known-degraded profile** is what turns a 15-second blip into a 5-minute outage. The failure path should not populate the cache.
2. **The failure is invisible.** Degrading silently is what makes this hard to diagnose from the outside.

Rated MEDIUM because a workaround exists once the cause is known. Worth noting it was observed without any attempt to provoke it.

Build `43579eb`.

Found during manual QA pass `QAT-PAY-D2`. Report: `docs/qat/reports/qat-payments-20260829.md` on branch `qa/manual-qat-20260829`.

## Summary

The "Completed" stat card on `/payments` hardcodes `'0'` whenever nothing is pending — so it reads zero precisely in the healthiest state.

## Observed

With 20 visible payment records all showing status "Paid":

| Card | Displayed |
|---|---|
| Total Collected | ₦17,034,053.00 (correct) |
| Completed / "Successful transactions" | **0** |
| Pending / "Awaiting payment" | 0 |
| Overdue / "Requires attention" | 0 |

Stable across two loads with a 20-second settle wait.

## Root cause

`src/app/(dashboard)/payments/page.tsx:85`

```tsx
<EnhancedStatCard
  title="Completed"
  value={stats.pending_count > 0 ? `${Math.max(0, (paymentsResult?.count || 0) - stats.pending_count)}` : '0'}
/>
```

The count is only computed when `pending_count > 0`; otherwise it returns the literal `'0'`. The guard looks inverted — the intended fallback for "no pending payments" is presumably the full count, not zero.

## Secondary: the `overdue` status is unreachable

The Overdue card can never be non-zero, because the enums disagree:

- `src/types/database.ts:770` — `status: 'paid' | 'pending' | 'failed'`
- `src/lib/validators/payment.ts:3` — `z.enum(['pending', 'paid', 'overdue', 'failed'])`

`getPaymentStats` (`src/actions/payments/get-payment-stats.ts:24-36`) counts `r.status === 'overdue'`, a value the `payment_records` schema does not admit. The validator will also accept an `'overdue'` status the database type does not model.

This is distinct from invoice overdue state, which works correctly. Arguably the card reading 0 is right given the schema — the defect is the enum drift, which is worth resolving in the same change.

`resetEmailImports` performs a global hard delete but has no `authorizePermission()` guard. Only RLS stands between a caller and the deletion.

## What it deletes

`src/actions/email-imports/reset-email-imports.ts` — all rows from `email_imports`, `email_messages` and `email_transactions`, plus any `payment_records` linked to them. When called **without** a `userId` parameter the scope is global, not user-scoped.

## The gap

The file imports and calls `logAudit` (line 4, line 148) but never calls `authorizePermission`. It uses `createServerSupabaseClient()` — the user-scoped client — so RLS is the only enforcement.

For comparison, the pattern `CLAUDE.md` documents as mandatory for write actions:

```ts
const auth = await authorizePermission(PERMISSIONS.MODULE_ACTION);
if (!auth.authorized) return { error: 'Unauthorized' };
```

## Why this looks like an oversight rather than a decision

`CLAUDE.md` records `email-imports/*` as intentionally permission-allowlisted, on the grounds that those flows are cron/webhook-driven or pre-auth and cannot take an admin RBAC guard.

`resetEmailImports` is neither. It is a UI-triggered admin action, wired through `useResetEmailImports` in `src/hooks/use-gmail-connection.ts` and surfaced on `/payments/email-imports`. It appears to have inherited a directory-wide exemption that does not fit it.

## Suggested fix

Add an explicit permission check (`EMAIL_IMPORTS_MANAGE` or similar), and remove this file from the `PERMISSION_ALLOWLIST` in `src/__tests__/integration/module-integration.test.ts` so the structural test enforces it going forward.

Worth confirming separately what RLS actually permits here for a non-admin role — that determines whether this is a latent hole or defence-in-depth that happens to hold.

Found during manual QA pass `QAT-SEC-18`. Report: `docs/qat/reports/qat-security-20260829.md` on branch `qa/manual-qat-20260829`.

## Summary

The "Generate Code → Permanent Code" action produces a code labelled **Permanent** that carries a concrete expiry — 23 hours for a Visitor-category contact — and is badged "Expiring Soon" at the moment it is created.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a security contact of category **Visitor**, e.g. `/security/contacts/e6a510dd-246b-40d2-b4e1-0fc3b6bfa814`.
2. Generate Code → **Permanent Code**.

## Actual

```
RES-RH7-56MQ
Permanent
Expiring Soon (23h)
Valid from 8/30/2026 to 8/31/2026
```

The badge says Permanent and Expiring Soon simultaneously. No "Uses" counter is shown (unlike one-time codes), and verification does succeed repeatedly — so the multi-use behaviour is correct.

## Root cause

`src/actions/security/codes.ts`, in `generateAccessCode`:

```ts
const categoryData = contact.category as unknown as { default_validity_days: number };
const validityDays = data.validity_days || categoryData?.default_validity_days || 30;

const validFrom = data.valid_from ? new Date(data.valid_from) : new Date();
const validUntil = data.valid_until
  ? new Date(data.valid_until)
  : new Date(validFrom.getTime() + validityDays * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
```

`validUntil` is computed from the category's `default_validity_days` **regardless of `code_type`**. There is no branch that exempts `permanent` from expiry. The Visitor category's default validity is 1 day (its edit form states "Default validity: 1 days (max: 30 days)"), so a "Permanent" code on a Visitor expires the next day.

Note a comment elsewhere in the same file reads `code_type: 'permanent', // Permanent but with validity limits`, which suggests "permanent" is intended to mean *multi-use* rather than *never expires*.

## Why this is worth fixing

If that is the intent, the UI is what is wrong: "Permanent" is the plain-English promise an operator relies on. A security officer issuing a permanent code to domestic staff or a long-term contractor would reasonably expect it to keep working, and would find it dead the following day with no warning at issue time.

Mitigating: the "Expiring Soon (23h)" badge is displayed right next to the label, so an attentive operator can see the contradiction. That is why this is Medium rather than higher — but a label and a badge that contradict each other on an access-control credential is a poor place to rely on attentiveness.

## Suggested fix

Either make `permanent` genuinely skip the expiry calculation, or rename the option to what it actually does (e.g. "Multi-use Code") and surface the resulting validity window in the generate menu before the code is issued.

## Summary

Visiting `/auth/verify-2fa` **with no session** renders a completely blank page — no form, no error, no redirect. The URL stays put.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Sign out (or use a browser with no Residio session).
2. Navigate to `http://localhost:3001/auth/verify-2fa`.
3. Wait for load.

## Actual

- `location.pathname` remains `/auth/verify-2fa` — no redirect occurs.
- `document.body.innerText` length is **0**. The only visible element is the floating "Residio Estate Assistant" chat widget, which is app chrome rather than page content.

- No JS crash. Console shows the normal provider sequence ending in `"No session found - initializing as Guest"`.

Those specific log entries did not recur on the clean repeat, but the blank page did.

## Contrast: the authenticated path works

Visiting the same route **while signed in** correctly redirects to `/dashboard` (verified separately). So the route has redirect handling for the has-session case, and no handling for the no-session case.
