Redirect to `/login`, consistent with every other protected route — an unauthenticated request to `/dashboard`, `/residents`, `/billing` etc. all redirect to `/login?next=…`.

## Impact

Narrow. A user only reaches this route mid-login with 2FA pending, so a direct unauthenticated visit is an edge case — which is why this is Low. But a blank page is the worst available failure mode: it gives the user nothing to act on and no indication whether the app is broken or their session simply expired. ## Summary

`https://meggarmind.github.io/RESIDIO/` has not updated since **2026-08-22**. The Docusaurus admin guide under `website/` has a deploy workflow, but it has never successfully published — the live site is a one-off manual push. Full findings are also recorded in `TODO.md` under *Admin User Guide → Docs site is stale — deploy automation never worked (revisit, 2026-09-01)* (commit `fb45a76`).

## Findings

### 1. GitHub Pages is in branch mode, not Actions mode — blocking

```
gh api repos/meggarmind/RESIDIO/pages
→ "build_type": "legacy", "source": { "branch": "gh-pages", "path": "/" }
```

`.github/workflows/deploy-admin-guide.yml` ends in `actions/deploy-pages@v4`, which **cannot publish while Pages is in branch mode**. Nothing else in the pipeline matters until this is flipped.

**Fix:** Settings → Pages → Source = "GitHub Actions" (or set `build_type: workflow` via the API). Requires repo admin, hence `ready-for-human`.

### 2. The deploy workflow has run exactly once, and it failed

Run `32586296177` (2026-08-22T16:57Z, on commit `docs: add deployable admin guide`) failed after 4 seconds. Logs have since expired.

**Next step:** re-run via `workflow_dispatch` to surface the real error. Suspect the `npm ci` cache path (`website/package-lock.json`) or the `npm run typecheck` step.

### 3. The live site is a manual one-off publish

`gh-pages` has only two commits, both from 2026-08-22:

```
9a77050 2026-08-22T17:01 deploy: fix admin guide base path
57c9c2b 2026-08-22T16:59 deploy: publish admin guide
```

Nothing has been pushed there since, which is why the site is frozen at that date.

### 4. There is no integrations page in the docs site — it was never committed

- `find website/docs -iname "*integration*"` → no results.
- `website/sidebars.ts` has 8 categories (Getting started, Residents, Properties, Finance, Security, Operations, Settings, Administration) — no Integrations entry.
- `git log --all` shows the only commit ever touching `website/` is `fa37650 docs: add deployable admin guide`.

The nearest existing content is `docs/features/gmail-integration.md`, which lives in the **repo docs** and is not part of the Docusaurus site. The integrations page needs to be located (unpushed worktree? another machine?) or rewritten before chasing the deploy.

### 5. Consider widening the workflow trigger

The workflow fires only on `website/**` and its own path. If repo docs under `docs/` should feed the site, that needs an added path filter or an explicit sync step.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pages source switched to GitHub Actions (`build_type: workflow`).
- [ ] `deploy-admin-guide.yml` completes green on `workflow_dispatch`, and the deployed URL reflects a fresh build.
- [ ] A push to `website/**` on `master` automatically updates the live site with no manual `gh-pages` step.
- [ ] Integrations page recovered or authored under `website/docs/`, added to `sidebars.ts`, and visible on the live site.

- Partial unique index on `(provider) WHERE is_active`.
- Reuse `src/lib/encryption.ts` (AES-256-GCM, `DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY`). Do not invent new crypto.

content.body:
Found by the reviewing session while pre-checking premises for #134, then verified. **This is a live bug today, independent of any planned change.**

> **Line numbers below are cited from `origin/master` (095c7e5).** An earlier revision of this issue carried numbers read from a working tree that already had edits in it, which put everything below line 124 three lines out. Verify against `git show origin/master:src/lib/notifications/send.ts`.

## The mechanism

`getSettingValue` (`src/actions/settings/get-settings.ts:62-63`) builds its client with `createServerSupabaseClient()` — user-scoped and RLS-bound. The `system_settings` SELECT policy is `TO authenticated` (`supabase/migrations/20251212215701_add_system_settings.sql:25-27`).

Cron routes run with **no authenticated user**, so that read matches zero rows and returns `null`. `if (error || !data) return null;` (`get-settings.ts:71`) then makes "row absent", "not authenticated" and "query errored" indistinguishable at every call site.

Every other data read in `src/lib/notifications/send.ts` correctly uses `createAdminClient()` — lines 147, 167, 178, 272, 363. The settings reads are the odd ones out in their own file.

## What breaks right now

Six `getSettingValue` calls in `send.ts` go through the RLS-bound path and return `null` under cron:

| Line | Setting | Consequence under cron |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 44 | `email_enabled` | Fails **open** — disabling email in the UI does not stop cron email |
| 70 | `email_from_name` | Falls back to `'Residio Estate'`, ignoring the configured name |
| 124 | `whatsapp_enabled` | Fails **open** — the master kill switch does nothing under cron |
| 137 | `whatsapp_outbound_daily_cap` | Always uses the compiled-in **100** |
| 161 | `whatsapp_outbound_burst_cap` | Always uses the compiled-in **20** |
| 163 | `whatsapp_outbound_burst_window_minutes` | Always uses the compiled-in **10** |

Note this is **not WhatsApp-only** — `email_enabled` has the identical shape.

## The caps are wrong in *both* directions

The precise failure is not that the cap vanishes under cron. It is that **cron always uses the compiled-in default regardless of what the admin configured**:

- Admin **lowers** the daily cap to 10 to contain a suspected defect → cron sends **100**. Fail-open; the bill-shock case.
- Admin **raises** it to 500 for a legitimate estate-wide broadcast → cron still stops at **100**. The broadcast silently truncates at 100 recipients with "daily outbound limit reached", while the admin's UI shows 500.
- Admin sets the cap to **0** to hard-stop outbound → `dailyCap <= 0` never fires under cron, because cron sees 100.

The second is the one nobody predicts; it will present as a random partial-delivery bug. In every case the admin UI and the sending path disagree and nothing surfaces it, because the admin's own browser session *is* authenticated and reads the row correctly.

PRD user story 30 asks for "software outbound/lookup caps in system settings, so that a defect can't cause bill shock or a broadcast storm." That control is **inert in both directions on the only path that matters.**

Affected cron routes: `process-notifications`, `payment-reminders`, `publish-announcements`.

## Why this blocks #134

#134 flips `whatsapp_enabled` to fail closed. Shipped without this fixed first, every cron-driven WhatsApp send dies silently while the admin UI shows the toggle ON — the error would read "disabled in system settings" while the setting says enabled. A miserable production debug, visible only in the cron path.

## Tasks

- Route settings reads used by server-side/cron paths through the service-role client, consistent with their five neighbours in `send.ts`. Add an admin-client variant of `getSettingValue`, or have it take an explicit client. **Do not** loosen the RLS policy on `system_settings` to work around it.
- **Distinguish "row absent" from "query errored".** Today `null` means both, plus "not authenticated". After a fail-closed change a transient Supabase error becomes an indistinguishable silent estate-wide outage. Decide deliberately what a read failure should do and make the code say so.
- Audit other `getSettingValue` callers reachable from unauthenticated cron or webhook contexts.
- Tests: a cron-path send honours a configured cap both **below** and **above** the default; an absent row is handled differently from a failed query.

## Acceptance

- With a non-default cap configured, a cron-driven send honours it — in both directions.
- Disabling email or WhatsApp in the UI actually stops cron sends.
- A query error is distinguishable from an absent row at the call site.

content.body:
Found by the reviewing session while checking #127's deployment safety, then verified across all three branches.

## The situation

`feat/social-login-approval-queue` carries **five** unapplied migrations, all timestamped `2026-08-30`:

```
20260830100000_add_impersonation_two_factor_permission_categories.sql
20260830100100_seed_missing_permission_catalog.sql
20260830100200_chairman_excludes_settings_module.sql
20260830100300_get_my_role_resolves_custom_roles.sql
20260830100400_rbac_writes_follow_manage_roles_permission.sql
```

None are on `master`. The cloud project's last applied migration is `20260830090000`, which matches `master` exactly — so there is **no drift on master**. An unmerged branch holding unapplied migrations is the normal case.

## The hazard

`feat/whatsapp-provider-config` (#127) adds `20260902080000_create_whatsapp_provider_credentials.sql`. When that is applied to cloud, the recorded migration history advances to `20260902080000`.

All five migrations above are timestamped **earlier** than that. Supabase orders migration history by version, so migrations arriving out of order are a known footgun: depending on how they are applied they either error, or are skipped as "already past that point" — leaving a migration that exists in git and never ran, with nothing reporting a failure.

That is the same failure shape as `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` silently keeping an old definition: **a file that looks applied and is not.**

## Why this one matters more than usual

Four of the five are RBAC and permissions changes — permission categories, the permission catalog seed, chairman module scope, `get_my_role()` resolving custom roles, and RBAC writes following the manage-roles permission. A permissions migration that silently does not run leaves the application code expecting a security posture the database does not have. That failure is invisible until someone is either wrongly denied access or wrongly granted it.

## What to do

Whichever lands second needs handling deliberately. Options, for whoever merges:

- Apply the five `2026-08-30` migrations **before** `20260902080000`, while the ordering is still natural.
- Or renumber them above `20260902080000` before merging `feat/social-login-approval-queue`.
- Or apply them explicitly and **verify each one actually ran** — do not infer success from a clean merge or a clean `db push`.

Whatever the route: after merging that branch, confirm the five migrations are present in the applied-migrations list by name, rather than trusting that the merge implies application.

## Not urgent

Nothing is broken today. `20260902080000` has not been applied yet either, so the ordering can still be resolved cleanly in either direction. It stops being cheap the moment one side is applied without the other.

#136 fixed the RLS-bound settings reads in `src/lib/notifications/send.ts` and the WhatsApp retention cron. While auditing callers for that issue, **eight more files were found with the identical bug**, all genuinely reachable from an unauthenticated cron or webhook context.

## The bug, restated

`getSettingValue` (`src/actions/settings/get-settings.ts`) reads through the user-scoped, RLS-bound client. `system_settings` grants SELECT `TO authenticated`. Cron routes and webhooks have no authenticated user, so **every settings read returns `null`** and each call site silently falls back to its compiled-in default.

This is not a WhatsApp problem. It is estate-wide.

## Files still affected

| File | Reached from | Impact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/actions/billing/apply-late-fees.ts` (6 reads) | `cron/apply-late-fees` | **Late-fee rules ignored.** Configured grace periods, rates and caps fall back to code defaults, so residents are charged on rules nobody set. |
| `src/actions/notifications/reminder-config.ts` (5 reads) + `invoice-reminders.ts` | `cron/payment-reminders` | Reminder escalation schedule and thresholds ignored. |
| `src/lib/email/send-email.ts` (3 reads) | `cron/process-report-schedules` | Email configuration ignored on the scheduled-report path. |
| `src/lib/notifications/invoice-generation-email.ts` | `cron/generate-invoices` | Invoice-email settings ignored. |
| `src/lib/sms/send-sms.ts` | `cron/payment-reminders` | SMS settings ignored (channel is dormant, so latent). |
| `src/lib/whatsapp/financial.ts` | WhatsApp inbound webhook | Financial-lookup daily cap ignored — the cap exists to bound disclosure volume. |
| `src/lib/whatsapp/rollout.ts` (3 reads) | WhatsApp inbound webhook, and `send.ts` | **Rollout gating ignored.** Pilot targeting and the estate-wide enable flag fall back to defaults on the webhook path. |

`apply-late-fees` is the one with money attached: it decides what residents are charged.

## Confirmed NOT affected

Checked and left alone, with reasons: `getCurrentDevelopmentLevyProfileId` (UI hook only), `api/receipts/[id]`, `api/statements` (both call `supabase.auth.getUser()` first, so the shared request cookies make the settings read authenticated too), `actions/email/send-welcome-email.ts`, `actions/email/send-payment-reminders.ts` (authenticated action callers only).

## Fix

Mechanical: swap to `getSettingValueAsService()` (added in #136), one file at a time, verifying each caller is genuinely server-side. Do **not** loosen the RLS policy on `system_settings` to work around it.

Where a setting is a safety control rather than a preference — the WhatsApp rollout gate, the financial-lookup cap, late-fee rules — consider whether an unreadable value should fail closed rather than fall back to a default, per the same reasoning as #134.

## Related

Found while auditing #136. Same root cause. The separate ungated-cron-route finding from the same audit is tracked separately.

`src/app/api/cron/process-report-schedules/route.ts` was a **public, unauthenticated GET**. It is registered in `vercel.json` as a daily cron (`0 7 * * *`) and calls `processDueSchedules()`, which generates scheduled reports and emails them to their subscribers.

Every other route in `src/app/api/cron/` gates on `verifyCronAuth(request)`, a timing-safe comparison against `CRON_SECRET`. This was the only exception — verified by scanning the whole directory.

## Impact

Anyone who knew or guessed the URL could trigger report generation and delivery repeatedly: compute and email cost, spam to whichever recipients each schedule targets, and delivery of report contents on demand rather than on schedule.

## Fix applied

Added the standard gate, matching every sibling route. Found while auditing settings reads for #136.

## Deployment note — read before deploying

`verifyCronAuth` returns **500 in production when `CRON_SECRET` is unset**. Since every other cron route already requires it, `CRON_SECRET` is presumably configured — but if it is not, this route was previously the only one still working, and adding the gate will stop it.

**Confirm `CRON_SECRET` is set in the production environment before deploying this.** Vercel Cron sends the `authorization` header automatically once the secret is configured.

```
20260829100000  add_profile_approval_status
```

## Why this is not cosmetic

**Master's migrations describe a database that does not exist**, and the gap is in authentication.

`20260829100200_gate_auth_helpers_on_approval_status.sql` redefines `get_my_role()` — the function ~100 RLS policies gate on. It adds an `approval_status = 'active'` requirement and removes the legacy `profiles.role` fallback. That is applied and live.

So anyone reading master to understand who can access what gets a materially wrong answer about the security posture of the live system.

While auditing authorisation on 2026-09-02, an exploration agent was asked for the current `get_my_role()`. It searched `supabase/migrations/`, correctly identified `20260106110000` as the latest definition **on that branch**, and quoted it. A second agent, reading a migration from the feature branch, quoted a different body. `CRON_SECRET` must be present in the production environment or **every scheduled job fails**. This is currently unverified: neither the maintainer nor the agent sessions can reach the Vercel dashboard, so this is filed as an outstanding task rather than a confirmed fault.

## Why it is now load-bearing

`verifyCronAuth()` (`src/lib/auth/cron-auth.ts:20-26`) fails closed:

```ts
if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' && !cronSecret) {
  console.error('[Cron] CRON_SECRET not configured in production');
  return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Server configuration error' }, { status: 500 });
}
```

Outside production it returns `null` and allows the request through, so **this cannot be reproduced locally** — a dev run will look healthy no matter what.

## Scope: all ten cron routes, not just #140's

Every route under `src/app/api/cron/` calls `verifyCronAuth`, verified by scanning the directory:

`apply-late-fees`, `fetch-emails`, `generate-invoices`, `generate-reports`, `payment-reminders`, `process-notifications`, `process-report-schedules`, `publish-announcements`, `refresh-payment-cadence`, `whatsapp-retention`.

Nine of those are scheduled in `vercel.json`. #140 closed the last unauthenticated route (`process-report-schedules`, fixed in `4153b75` on `master`), which is correct and should stay — but it also means a missing secret is now fatal for the whole set rather than one route.

## Correction to an earlier framing

This was previously described as a 07:00 UTC deadline, taken from `process-report-schedules`. That is the wrong first failure. Per `vercel.json`, `publish-announcements` and `fetch-emails` run at `0 * * * *` — **hourly**. If the secret is missing in production, the first 500s appear within the hour, not at 07:00. Full schedule:

| Schedule | Route |
|---|---|
| `0 * * * *` | publish-announcements, fetch-emails |
| `0 0 * * *` | refresh-payment-cadence |
| `15 0 * * *` | whatsapp-retention |
| `0 6 * * *` | generate-invoices, generate-reports |
| `0 7 * * *` | process-report-schedules |
| `0 8 * * *` | payment-reminders |
| `0 9 * * *` | process-notifications |

## Failure signature

Silent from the user's side. Invoices are not generated, reminders and scheduled reports are not emailed, announcements do not publish, notifications do not drain. The only evidence is a 500 and `[Cron] CRON_SECRET not configured in production` in the platform logs.

## Deployment target is not settled

**Final production deployment may not be Vercel.** `vercel.json` is the only schedule definition in the repo, so if hosting moves, the nine schedules move with it and do not carry over automatically. Any replacement platform needs both the `CRON_SECRET` env var and its own scheduler invoking these paths with `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>`. Worth resolving as part of the hosting decision rather than after it.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Confirm `CRON_SECRET` is set in the production environment (or in whichever platform ends up hosting)
- [ ] Confirm the scheduler sends `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>`
- [ ] Confirm at least one scheduled run returns 200 in the platform logs
- [ ] If hosting is not Vercel, port all nine `vercel.json` schedules to the target platform

## Notes

Requires infrastructure access that agent sessions do not have; it cannot be closed from the codebase. Filed per maintainer instruction after the check was found to be unperformable in-session.

Two machines run Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex against this repo, sometimes concurrently. Nothing prevented two of them editing the same branch, and `docs/agents/session-roles.md` declared itself two-party and refused a role to any third session — excluding most of the real workstreams.

Every incident today was **caught by cross-checking, not prevented**: a branch whose name disagreed with its upstream, a Stop-hook checkpoint pushing 834 unreviewed lines onto a feature branch, six migrations applied in production with no file on master, five more queued to arrive out of order, and a P0-causing migration withheld by a record living only in files the next reader might not open.

## What this adds

**`docs/agents/branching.md`** — the rules every session shares, whatever its tool:
- Never work on `master`. It is a merge target; a rejected push is the rule working, not a bug to route around, and asking another session to push for you is the same bypass in disguise.
- Branch prefixes declare the lane — `codex/issue-<n>-<slug>`, `feat/<slug>`, `fix/<slug>`, `qa/<date>`, `merge/<slug>`.
- **A branch name is not evidence of its upstream.** Report `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{upstream}`, not the name — that exact mismatch produced a false push-safety claim today.
- Sync `master` in *before* work that isn't central to the feature.
- Migrations ride the branch that introduces them. Never apply one to "close a gap in the sequence" — the gap is usually deliberate and its record may not be on your branch.
- Declare tool, branch and intent in `SESSION_STATE.md`; check it before taking a branch.
- The `stage` contract, and how to roll back through it.

**`AGENTS.md`** carries the summary, because all three tools read it (`CLAUDE.md:5` already names it the shared source of truth). **`CLAUDE.md`** gets a pointer only — no duplication.

**`docs/agents/session-roles.md`** — rewrites `## Sessions outside the arrangement`. Rex/Quinn becomes one named arrangement rather than the only legitimate configuration; other sessions are referred to the branching rules instead of turned away. The consent-surface separation is kept.

**`.github/workflows/stage-backup.yml`** — `stage` advances to `master` only when install, test and build are green. The rollback point is therefore always a *verified* master, not merely a previous one. Nothing pushes to `stage` by hand.

**`package-lock.json`** — synced to `package.json`'s `0.4.0`; the version was bumped without regenerating the lockfile.

## Enforcement

Docs bind tools that read them. Branch protection on `master` (strict, no admin bypass) is being enabled separately and binds every tool, machine and fresh container regardless. Git hooks were considered and declined — they need per-clone setup and `--no-verify` defeats them.

- `npx vitest run` — **369 passed, 65 suites**, unchanged
- `git diff --cached --check` — clean
- `stage-backup.yml` parses as valid YAML

Two defects in the guardrails from #152, both found in review. Both are mine.

## 1. The session-start declaration rule could not be complied with

`branching.md` §5 required declaring tool, branch and intent in `SESSION_STATE.md` at session start. `SESSION_STATE.md` lives on `master`. §1 and branch protection forbid writing to `master`. So a declaration needed a PR that only becomes visible **once merged** — by which point the coordination window it exists to protect has closed.

The repo's coordination file was the one file the coordination rules forbade writing to. By `session-roles.md`'s own standing term — *do not queue work under a term the other side cannot run* — the rule was unrunnable, and it bound every session.

**Fix:** the live registry is the remote branch list.

```bash
git ls-remote --heads origin      # who is working on what, right now
```

Push your branch early — **the push is the declaration**. The prefix names the lane, the name names the work, and it is visible to every tool on every machine instantly with no PR in the way. `SESSION_STATE.md` stays the end-of-session **handoff record**; that is a record rather than a signal, and a PR is the right speed for it.

Corrected in `branching.md` §5, `AGENTS.md`, and `SESSION_STATE.md` coordination rule 6, which all carried the same wrong instruction.

## 2. The `stage` diagnostic inverts under the condition it is actually in

§6 said: *"If `stage` lags, the commits between them have not passed."* That reads as **master is bad**. The truth right now is that the gate **never executed**.

**GitHub Actions is locked account-wide.** Verified across four different workflows — Stage backup, Admin Guide Drift, Deploy Residio Admin Guide — every run fails in ~2 seconds with **0 steps** and the identical annotation:

> `The job was not started because your account is locked due to a billing issue.`

All 40 most recent runs failed. Issue #126, filed yesterday, reports the Pages deploy has *never* worked — same cause.

Those two states demand opposite responses: *investigate the commits* versus *fix the runner*. The doc now distinguishes them with a table, gives the two commands that tell them apart, and records the current lock so a lagging `stage` is read as **unverified rather than failed**.

Same failure class as a migrations directory describing a database it cannot observe — an artefact reporting a state it has no way to see.

## Consequences worth stating plainly

While the lock holds, **`stage` cannot advance at all** and is pinned at `30a4dac`. Branch protection still enforces ordering, but with `required_approving_review_count: 0` and no status checks able to run, **nothing verifies what merges**. The gate is real; it is currently gating on nothing.

Docs only — no source, migration or workflow changes.

The lock had been masking four real problems. This PR fixes three; the fourth needs repository secrets.

## 1. Stage gate blocker — `pathsMatch` was platform-dependent

`resolve()` treats `\` as a path separator on Windows and as an ordinary character on POSIX, so `pathsMatch('C:/repo/.worktrees/issue-64', 'C:\repo\.worktrees\issue-64')` returned `true` on Windows and `false` on the Linux runner. The suite passed locally while `Stage backup` failed, leaving `stage` **31 commits behind master**. Now normalises separators on both sides and case-folds the drive letter.

## 2. Issue monitor read board cards from the wrong repository

Project #1 is shared by three repos (RESIDIO 100 cards, `tomtracker` 14, `CMBVsaq` 11). Issue numbers are per-repository, so several cards are numbered 13. `issueItem()` matched on the number alone:

```js
items.find((item) => Number(item.content?.number) === Number(issueNumber))
```

RESIDIO #13 is CLOSED and **not on the board at all**, but the monitor read its status from `CMBVsaq#13` (Backlog) and reported `closed-not-done`. All 15 such findings were this artefact.

Not merely a reporting fault — `writeFinding()` calls `gh issue edit --add-label` and `gh issue comment` with the RESIDIO checkout as `cwd`. The first successful scheduled run would have **labelled and commented on ~15 RESIDIO issues on the strength of another project's cards**. It has never run only because `ISSUE_WORKFLOW_PAT` is unset.

Verified against the live board:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `closed-not-done` | 15 | **0** |
| issues processed | 108 | 91 = 100 cards − 9 PRs |
| genuine RESIDIO cards dropped | — | **0** |

The 17 dropped numbers all belong to other repositories, and **#16 — which exists in both RESIDIO and CMBVsaq — keeps its RESIDIO card**, confirming the filter matches by URL rather than number. Covered by a regression test including draft cards with no URL and a look-alike host.

## 3. Node 20 deprecation

All five workflows ran on actions GitHub already force-migrates to Node 24. Bumped to the first node24 major of each. `add-to-project` v2 changes no inputs — its release notes are dependency bumps plus the runtime. The `setup-node` `node-version` inputs are untouched; those pin the Node the app builds against and are a separate decision.

## Problem

The stage gate's `Build` step failed on every push to `master`, blocking `stage` from advancing:

```
Error occurred prerendering page "/settings/audit-logs"
Error: @supabase/ssr: Your project's URL and API key are required to create a Supabase client!
```

This was masked until #157 landed — the `Test` step failed first, so the gate never reached `Build`.

## Cause

The step set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. `src/lib/supabase/config.ts` never reads either. It reads **suffixed** names chosen by `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENV_MODE`:

```ts
const envMode = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_ENV_MODE || 'local';
url: envMode === 'local'
  ? process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL_LOCAL!
  : process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL_CLOUD!,
```

So the placeholders landed nowhere and the client was constructed with `undefined`. The `!` non-null assertions hide that at compile time; it surfaces at prerender.

## Fix

Use the names the app reads, and pin `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENV_MODE` so which pair is read is explicit rather than resting on the `'local'` default. Adds the service-role placeholder for server components that build an admin client during prerender.

**Placeholders only.** Nothing in this step contacts Supabase, and no real credential belongs in a workflow file.

## Verification

Ran the full build locally with exactly these four variables. It completes, and the page that was failing emits output with no prerender errors anywhere in the build:

```
.next/server/app/(dashboard)/settings/audit-logs/page.js
```

This failure is environment-variable naming, which resolves identically on Linux — unlike the path-portability bug in #157, where the platform was the bug itself. CI on merge is the final confirmation.

## Expected result

`Build` passes, the gate goes green end to end, and `stage` advances for the first time since it fell behind.

Note: `Monitor issue workflow` will still fail — `ISSUE_WORKFLOW_PAT` is not configured. Unrelated to this PR.

content.body:
## Problem

The issue monitor's first successful live dry run (2026-09-02) reported:

```
Summary: healthy=36  stale=21  inconsistent=48  suppressed=0  failures=0
```

**Twenty-four of the 48 `inconsistent` findings are `done-no-integration` on issues that closed cleanly through merged PRs** — including #138, #143, #144, #145, #146, #147 and #142, all closed the same day via merged pull requests with the work verifiably on `master`.

Two dozen simultaneously-broken closures is not the likely explanation. The likely explanation is that `integrationEvidence` in `scripts/issue-monitor.mjs` does not recognise a merged PR as integration evidence in the shape these issues have.

Note the contrast in the same report: #126, #141 and #147 came back **healthy**, and #126's evidence line reads `PR #157`. So PR evidence is detected in *some* shapes and not others — worth finding what separates them.

## Why it blocks the rollout

The hourly `schedule:` trigger runs **without** `--dry-run`, so enabling it writes a `needs-attention` label and an evidence comment on every flagged issue. Sweeping while half the findings are false positives would label correctly-closed issues and train everyone to ignore the label.

The schedule is therefore **held** — commented out in `.github/workflows/monitor-issue-workflow.yml` with the rationale inline (PR #161). `workflow_dispatch` with dry-run still works.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `done-no-integration` does not fire on an issue closed via a merged PR whose branch landed on `master`.
- [ ] Determine why #126/#141/#147 were detected as healthy while #138/#143–#147 were not, and make detection consistent.
- [ ] A dispatch at `dry_run=true` shows the `done-no-integration` count reduced to genuine cases only.
- [ ] Tests cover merged-PR integration evidence, including the closure shapes that currently miss.
- [ ] Re-enable the `schedule:` trigger in the same change, and record the first live sweep's result.

## Not in scope

The 21 `stale-active` findings appear genuine — #7, #8, #59, #60, #61 sit in `In review` with ~219h of inactivity, matching abandoned Codex worktrees still on disk. Those are real drift and should be triaged separately, not suppressed.

## Context

`ISSUE_WORKFLOW_PAT` is configured and working. `read:org` was the missing scope behind the earlier `unknown owner type` failure — `project` and `public_repo` alone are not sufficient, because `gh` classifies the `--owner` login before it reads the project.

Tracking issue for the Settings information-architecture work. Design settled by interview on 2026-09-02; decisions recorded in `docs/adr/0004`, `0005`, `0006` and vocabulary in `CONTEXT.md` (branch `feat/settings-ia-docs`).

## The problem

Settings grew to 6 groups and ~34 links with **no stated grouping rule**. That is the root cause, not a symptom — without a rule, the WhatsApp operations console landed under "General & Preferences" and Gmail import under "Billing & Finance", and nothing prevents the next feature landing somewhere equally arbitrary.

Investigated and found:
- `/settings/system` is **not broken** — verified in-browser as super_admin: 200, no redirect, full content, no console errors. The real problem is that landing on `/settings` shows only **12 of 34** links, because five of six groups start collapsed.
- Settings does two unrelated jobs: things you *set* beside things you *watch*.
- Three surfaces show the same cron data via two fetch paths; the Gmail pages are near-identical; the notification queue exists twice via **two independent backends**.
- Global search cannot find settings at all.
- Chairman's exclusion from Settings never actually held.

## The rule

**Settings groups by subject/module**, matching the main sidebar. Settings holds **configuration and reference data only**; operational surfaces move to a new `System` section at `/system/*`. **Integrations is the one stated exception** — grouped by the service connected rather than the subject served, and exempt from the configuration-only boundary, because an integration is something you connect, tune and watch in one place.

## Read first

**#167 blocks every `/system` slice and is not optional.** Middleware is the only auth gate for the dashboard, and when no `ROUTE_PERMISSIONS` key matches it skips the auth block entirely rather than denying. A `/system/*` page shipped without its own entry is **fully public**.

## Slices

| # | Slice | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|
| #167 | Middleware safety net | — |
| #168 | Chairman regains `settings.view` | — |
| #169 | Main sidebar loses submenu state on every navigation | — |
| #170 | Reopen collapsed group on entry; mobile multi-open | — |
| #171 | Audit logs to `/system/audit-logs` (template slice) | #167 |
| #172 | Account administration to `/system/accounts` | #167 |
| #173 | Consolidate the two notification queue backends | #167 |
| #174 | Canonical cron page + **close the public cron API** | #167 |
| #175 | Ownership backfill to `/system/data-tools` | #167 |
| #176 | Rename `/settings/system/*` | #167, before #178 |
| #177 | New `/system` health dashboard | #171–#176 |
| #178 | Regroup Settings into six groups; merge Gmail pages | #171–#176 |
| #179 | Index Settings and System in the Cmd+K palette | #178 |

#168, #169 and #170 are fully independent and can ship immediately.

## Separate defects found on the way

#163 (`prettier` undeclared — breaks tests and the dev server), #164 (palette has no permission filtering), #165 (`search_logs` written but never read), #166 (Cmd+1–5 shortcuts jump to the wrong result).

## Outcomes

1. Every Settings page has one obvious home, because there is a written rule and only one stated exception to it.
2. Settings holds only things you change; things you watch get a section of their own.
3. An Integrations group exists, with obvious room for Paystack and SMS.
4. Typing "email import" into Cmd+K goes straight to the page, and search never shows a page your role cannot open.
5. Settings shrinks from ~34 links to ~24, six groups, depth 2.
6. Group expansion survives navigation and reload, and a group reopens when you enter it, so the page you are on is never hidden.
7. Mobile and desktop menus behave identically.
8. Cron health, the notification queue and the Gmail connection each have exactly one page instead of three, two and two.
9. Chairman can open Settings again, seeing only areas they already had permission for.
10. An unauthenticated stranger can no longer read the estate's cron status.
11. Every old URL still works, via permanent redirects.
12. Two ADRs and four glossary entries let the next person place a new setting without asking.
